transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

I understand how frustrating this is after a power cut. Since the machine is completely dead with no lights at all, and we know the plug fuse is fine, the most likely cause is that the internal mains interference filter (the first component electricity hits inside the machine) has failed due to the surge from the power cut. Before we assume the worst, we need to rule out a simple supply issue. Could you please plug a different, working appliance (like a lamp or phone charger) into that same washing machine socket to confirm it has power? This is quick and safe.
Yes, I tried a lamp in that socket and it works fine. Washer-dryer is still completely dead though.

[Heading: Likely cause: mains filter]
Since the socket has power but the washer-dryer is completely dead, the most likely cause is that the internal mains interference filter (the first component electricity hits inside the machine) has blown due to the surge from the power cut. Before we assume that, please do this quick check:
1. Unplug the machine from the wall socket.
2. Check that the plug is pushed fully into the socket and examine the lead for any cuts or damage.
3. If it looks fine, plug it back in firmly. If it still has no lights after reseating the plug, we can be fairly confident the filter has failed. To help me identify the correct replacement part, could you please tell me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I unplugged it and the plug and lead look fine, no damage. Left it unplugged over 10 minutes earlier and plugged back in firmly, still dead. The model number on the label is CSOW 4965TWE/1-80.

[Heading: Likely cause: mains filter]
Since the socket is live and the plug/lead are fine, the surge from the power cut has probably blown the internal mains interference filter. This is a standard safety component that sits right where the cable enters the machine; it sacrifices itself to protect the electronics. 1. 2. I have your model (CSOW 4965TWE/1-80), but I cannot confirm the exact part number or availability for this specific variant. Your best options are to contact Candy customer support with that model number to order the correct mains filter, or call a local engineer who can source and fit it safely.
